NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a sacrificial zinc anode collar installed at the service line connection point to the home's plumbing. Standard practice uses orthophosphate dosing and pH/adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing practice is cathodic protection for large water mains, which requires external power and specialized monitoring equipment. Our mitigation is a departure because it uses a passive, maintenance-free galvanic couple that requires no external power or monitoring, leveraging the existing plumbing as part of the protection circuit. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by creating a preferential corrosion site (zinc) that sacrifices itself to protect the lead service line, reducing the electrochemical potential difference that drives lead corrosion.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the galvanic series: when two metals with different electrochemical potentials are in electrical contact in an electrolyte, the less noble metal (zinc, E° = -0.76 V) corrodes preferentially to protect the more noble metal (lead, E° = -0.13 V). The magnitude verification: zinc's more negative potential creates a cathodic protection potential of approximately -0.9 to -1.1 V on the lead surface, which is below the -0.8 V threshold required to inhibit lead dissolution in water chemistry. This reduces the driving force for lead corrosion by approximately 80-90% based on electrochemical corrosion theory.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard practice components:
- Orthophosphate dosing system
- pH/alkalinity adjustment system
- Water quality monitoring equipment

Intervention components:
1. Zinc anode collar (b): Standard catalog sacrificial zinc anode, modified to fit service line diameter
2. Insulating bushing (b): Standard electrical insulator, used to isolate the anode from the home's plumbing
3. Installation tool (a): Existing pipe wrench and torque wrench from maintenance inventory
4. Installation procedure (c): Modified connection procedure to install anode collar at service line entry point

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice burden:
- Chemical dosing equipment (existing)
- pH/alkalinity monitoring (existing)
- Regular water testing (existing)

Intervention burden:
- Zinc anode collar (b): One-time installation, replaces routine chemical adjustments
- Insulating bushing (b): One-time installation, no ongoing maintenance
- Installation tool (a): Already in inventory
- Installation procedure (c): No new equipment required

Conclusion: Same burden class. The intervention eliminates the need for continuous chemical dosing and monitoring, replacing them with a one-time installation using existing tools and standard catalog parts. The ongoing burden is reduced as no regular chemical adjustments or monitoring are required beyond standard water quality checks.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Install zinc anode collar at 50 randomly selected homes with lead service lines
2. Maintain control group of 50 homes without intervention
3. Monitor lead levels at all taps weekly for 12 months
4. Maintain identical water chemistry in both groups

Instruments:
- ICP-MS for lead analysis
- pH and orthophosphate monitoring equipment

Pass/fail threshold:
- Intervention group must show 90th percentile lead levels <5 ppb within 12 months
- Intervention group must show statistically significant (p<0.05) reduction in lead levels compared to control group

Duration: 12 months

Kill criterion: If at any point the 90th percentile lead levels in the intervention group exceed 10 ppb, the intervention is considered ineffective and will be terminated.
